candidateEvidence.excerpt: Anthropic announced Claude Opus 5.5 on September 22. With the launch, it says it raised five-hour usage limits on Pro, Max, Team and seat-based Enterprise plans. Subscription users also get a rate-limit reset they can save for later.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: Claude Opus 5.5 — September 22, 2026. Claude Opus 5.5 is now available on all platforms, including Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure.

scopeAndFreshness: P002 states the September 22 announcement; the source page heading 'Claude Opus 5.5 — September 22, 2026' supplies exactly that date, checked September 26.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: For developers paying Anthropic directly for API use — a software connection to a model — input costs $4 and output $20 per million tokens. Those are usage charges based on text processed, not monthly Claude subscription prices.
If you pay Anthropic directly for API usage, the token table is your meter. Anthropic’s performance, speed, safety and cost-per-task claims are not independently validated here.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: Input and output tokens are $4 and $20 per million, 20% less than Opus 5. Cache reads (which make up the majority of agentic and coding work costs) are $0.20 per million tokens, 60% less than Opus 5.

scopeAndFreshness: P004's $4 input / $20 output per million tokens matches the source excerpt verbatim, and the article correctly frames these as direct API usage charges, not subscription prices.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: Anthropic announced Claude Opus 5.5 on September 22. With the launch, it says it raised five-hour usage limits on Pro, Max, Team and seat-based Enterprise plans. Subscription users also get a rate-limit reset they can save for later.
A usage limit is the amount a plan lets you use within a stated time window. The announcement does not quantify those limits or map ordinary Claude-chat model-selector access plan by plan.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: In addition to the price drop, we’re increasing five-hour usage limits on Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans. We’re also providing subscription users a rate limit reset, which you can now save and use whenever you choose.

scopeAndFreshness: P002 mirrors the source: five-hour limits raised on Pro, Max, Team and seat-based Enterprise, plus a saveable rate-limit reset, attributed with 'it says'; P003 preserves the source limitation that limits are not quantified.
